{{short description|Japanese learned society}}
The '''Mathematical Society of Japan''' ('''MSJ''', {{langx|ja|日本数学会}}) is a [[learned society]] for mathematics in [[Japan]].

In 1877, the organization was established as the ''Tokyo Sugaku Kaisha'' and was the first academic society in Japan. It was re-organized and re-established in its present form in 1946.

The MSJ has roughly 5,000 members.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mathsoc.jp/en/pamph/current/president.html|title=Greetings from the President|first=Seiichi|last=Kamada|year=2020|publisher=Mathematical Society of Japan|access-date=2024-05-13}}</ref> They have the opportunity to participate in programs at MSJ meetings which take place in spring and autumn each year. They also have the opportunity to announce their own research at these meetings.

==Prizes==
===Iyanaga Prize===
The '''Iyanaga Prize''' was a mathematics award granted by the Mathematical Society of Japan.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mathsoc.jp/en/list/winners-list.html |title=List of Spring and Autumn Prizes Winners |website=Mathematical Society of Japan |access-date=14 March 2023}}</ref> The prize was funded through an endowment given by [[Shokichi Iyanaga]].<ref>{{MacTutor |class=Societies |id=Japanese |title=Mathematical Society of Japan |date=February 2018}}</ref> Since 1988, it has been replaced by the [[#Spring Prize|Spring Prize]].
* 1973 - [[Yasutaka Ihara]]
* 1974 - [[Reiko Sakamoto (mathematician)|Reiko Sakamoto]]
* 1975 - [[Motoo Takahashi]]
* 1976 - {{ill|Mitsuyoshi Katō|de}}
* 1977 - [[Takahiro Kawai]]

===Geometry Prize===
The '''Geometry Prize''' is a mathematics award granted by the Mathematical Society of Japan to recognise significant or long-time research work in the field of [[geometry]], including [[differential geometry]], [[topology]], and [[algebraic geometry]]. It was established in 1987<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mathsoc.jp/section/geometry/en/prize-e.html |title=MSJ Geometry Prize |website=Mathematical Society of Japan |access-date=19 January 2025}}</ref> by [[Morio Obata]].<ref name="Nagano">{{cite conference | last=Nagano | first=Tadashi | last2=Omori | first2=Hideki | last3=Maeda | first3=Yoshiaki | last4=Kanai | first4=Masahiko | title=Geometry and its Applications; In Honor of Morio Obata: Proceedings of the Workshop | publisher=World Scientific | date=1993 | isbn=978-981-02-1205-6 | doi=10.1142/9789814536479 | url=http://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/9789814536479 | access-date=2025-07-22| url-access=subscription }}</ref>

===Takebe Prize===
In the context of its 50th anniversary celebrations, the Mathematical Society of Japan established the Takebe Prize for the encouragement of those who show promise as mathematicians.  The award is named after [[Edo period]] mathematician {{nihongo|[[Takebe Kenkō|Takebe Katahiro]]|建部賢弘||1664-1739}} (also known as Takebe Kenkō).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mathsoc.jp/en/pamph/current/takebe_pr.html |title=The MSJ Takebe Katahiro Prize |website=Mathematical Society of Japan |access-date=14 March 2023}}</ref>

==English Publications from MSJ==
MSJ publishes the following journals in English.
* Journal of the Mathematical Society of Japan (JMSJ)<ref>[https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.jmsj Journal of the Mathematical Society of Japan, Publication Information], [[Project Euclid]].</ref>
* Japanese Journal of Mathematics (JJM)<ref>[https://www.ms.u-tokyo.ac.jp/~toshi/jjm/JJMJ/JJM_JHP/jjm-index_jp.htm Japanese Journal of Mathematics].</ref><ref>[https://www.springer.com/mathematics/journal/11537 Japanese Journal of Mathematics], Springer.</ref>
* ''Publications of the Mathematical Society of Japan''<ref>[https://press.princeton.edu/catalogs/series/title/publications-of-the-mathematical-society-of-japan.html Publications of the Mathematical Society of Japan], [[Princeton University Press]].</ref>
* ''Advanced Studies in Pure Mathematics''<ref>[https://www.worldscientific.com/series/aspm Advanced Studies in Pure Mathematics], [[World Scientific]].</ref>
* ''MSJ Memoirs''<ref>[https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.msjm MSJ Memoirs], [[Project Euclid]].</ref><ref>[http://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~kenkyubu/kashiwara/memoirs.html MSJ Memoirs, Mathematical Society of Japan].</ref>
